Celsius framed at the center of an energy-category 'renaissance' - new consumers, especially females, entering for the first time and need-state lines blurring (energy consumed throughout the day and with meals).

Management candidly acknowledged Celsius slipped from a ~12.3% 2024 US share peak to ~10.8-11% - 'not pleased with that' - driven by 2024's front-loaded innovation being cycled and unusually heavy Red Bull/Monster sugar-free innovation vs. Celsius's lighter 2025 calendar.
Convenience-channel under-indexing is the single biggest US share opportunity - Celsius + Alani Nu represent almost 25% of MULO large-format share while Alani is barely present in convenience.

The two-brand portfolio's #1 advantage is pricing/promotional optionality (high-low strategies, timing/sequencing) in a highly promotional category; brand/marketing teams kept separate to preserve each brand's identity.

Celsius runs low-50s gross margin and low-30s SG&A; Alani Nu expected to converge over a two-year integration, with $50M of synergies on top; the company is comfortable with the $50M whether the North American distribution is dual or single.

Distribution uncertainty left explicitly unresolved - whether Alani Nu moves from ABI into PepsiCo; 'there's been no decisions on the path forward,' though PepsiCo's CEO referenced active discussions.

Synergy harvest concentrated in 2026 - the 12-month Congo Brands TSA and a methodical headcount/supply-chain transition push most capture into 2026; optionality to capture sooner if opportunities arise.
First-ever Celsius LTO (winter theme) in the back half of 2025, designed to attract new consumers and disrupt the path to purchase; new holistic 'Live Fit / Fit Go' marketing campaign launched.

Alani Nu's largest-ever innovation year (2025) includes Witch's Brew for Halloween and a winter edition; Alani revenue is LTO-driven and lumpy (a launch followed by ~60 days of pickup then trail-off; pipe-fill recorded then a couple-week delay before it hits scanner data).

Celsius is now a ~$100M international business growing off a small base - ~88% ACV in France, mid-teens share in Sweden, gaining share in Finland; recently launched France, Australia, NZ, Benelux, UK; partnered with Suntory; goal to break even in ~3-5 years and aspire to a 10 share.

International approach is tactical - not over-investing, building trial then investing more; considering bringing Alani Nu to Sweden where Celsius is more established; same global health/wellness, sugar-free, female trends apply.

Energy category growing over 10% recently, high single digits expected forward; sourcing volume from softness in tea, water, juice and coffee; GLP-1 cited as a broadening tailwind for better-for-you energy and protein.

SKU rationalization is continuous - SKU consistency is 'a big opportunity' (flavors vary by retailer); shifting from regional 'lead launches' toward national launches; rebalancing pack sizes (upsizing 12-packs, reducing 4-packs) as consumption shifts to large-format pantry purchasing.

Adjacency optionality: powders/hydration (hydration launched in Walmart), Alani Nu's ~$50M RTD protein business (somewhat lower margin, improves with scale, under evaluation); Celsius has a 'right to play' in hydration adjacencies.

Capital allocation: ~$450M cash remains after paying ~$450M toward the acquisition; the company is cash-generative and CapEx-light, will pay down 'some' (not all) acquisition debt to build credit; M&A optionality on the balance sheet.
Big Beverage (acquired 2024, mostly Celsius product) being expanded with a second line over 15-18 months, eventually bringing ~20% of combined production in-house - a forward margin lever.
Energy is a highly impulse-driven category - being within six feet of a register matters; two brands give greater retailer leverage for shelf space and cooler strategies.
Introduce the company - Celsius is newer/less familiar to European investors despite ~88% ACV in France.

An energy-category renaissance: Celsius was born in the US as a fitness, sugar-free, functional-vitamin (seven essential vitamins) brand, now joined by female-focused Alani Nu. New consumers - especially females - entering for the first time, consumption occasions expanding to throughout-the-day and with-meals. Cited Subway (up to 20,000 locations), Jersey Mike's, the PepsiCo partnership, foodservice meal-pairing, and a refreshing flavor lineup.
Alani Nu's Effect on Company Identity
How adding Alani Nu evolves the company's identity internally and in the marketplace.

Internally, the company has built a capable infrastructure (supply, procurement, sales, finance) and Alani Nu drives synergies. In the marketplace, a single brand competing at a high level faces pricing/promotional challenges; a multi-brand portfolio (core Celsius, Essentials, Alani Nu) enables a portfolio approach with competitive advantages and ~16-16.5% combined category share.
How the company defines and sizes the addressable market, given its brands differ from traditional Monster/Red Bull.

The historical heavy consumer was male 25-34, but the category is now gender- and age-balanced, with sugar-free above 50% of North America category sales for the first time last year. Celsius is 'increasing the pie,' targeting 18-34 while also aging up as consumers seek healthier alternatives.
Level-set the pro forma financial profile of the combined business and how the synergies layer in.

Celsius's pre-Alani profile is low-50s gross margin and low-30s SG&A; Alani Nu expected to converge over a two-year integration, with $50M of synergies on top driving further margin expansion, plus additional leverage and global expansion.
Why synergies ramp mostly in the first half of 2026 and why the harvest is concentrated in a couple of quarters.

Synergies bucket into supply chain and people. A 12-month TSA with Congo Brands covers the employee base; a separate marketing team/head was carved out. Moving Alani Nu's supply chain into Celsius's orbit model and transitioning headcount happen over the 12 months as two work streams. Gross-margin benefit comes as the supply chain is fully integrated (some sooner, some in the back half of 2026); finance/IT/back-shop synergies at the tail end; sales timing depends on commercial-strategy sequencing - the lowest-risk, methodical approach, with optionality to capture sooner.
U.S. Category Lag & Drivers of YTD Performance
Drivers of Celsius's year-to-date lag versus the growing US category, and the enablers of a return to growth.

Celsius peaked at ~12.3% US category share in 2024, now ~10.8-11%. The company front-loaded 2024 innovation (now cycling) and took a more balanced 2025 approach; first Celsius LTO in the back half. 2024 saw the heaviest-ever Red Bull/Monster sugar-free innovation activity, against which Celsius's lighter calendar underperformed. Cited the new 'Live Fit / Fit Go' campaign, Alani Nu's largest-ever innovation year (Witch's Brew, winter edition), and the portfolio's ability to drive new-to-category consumers.
Aspirational market-share objectives for Celsius vs. Alani Nu, and Celsius's aspirational margin.

At ~11% share the company is 'not pleased' and sees huge US upside - markets with a level playing field (Amazon, South Florida, NYC, LA) near or above 20% share. The biggest opportunity is closing the convenience-channel gap where Celsius is under-indexed; Celsius + Alani Nu represent almost 25% of MULO large-format share while Alani is barely in convenience. Cited food-pairing trial-driving deals (Casey's, NYC).
How the international growth journey plays out, the level of prioritization vs. US opportunities, and how Alani Nu layers in.

International a huge opportunity (Monster's international success, global health/wellness trends). Celsius has a mid-teens Sweden share, gains in Finland, recently launched France, Australia, NZ, Benelux, UK (partnered with Suntory); France ~88% ACV. Tactical approach - not over-investing, building trial then investing more - goal to break even in ~3-5 years and aspire to a 10 share. International a ~$100M business in 2025. Alani Nu international entry is a timing question - considering Sweden first.
How the Two Brands Work Together
How Celsius and Alani Nu complement each other in the marketplace and whether managing two brands creates conflicts/complexity.

The portfolio's #1 advantage is pricing/promotional optionality (high-low strategies, timing/sequencing) in a highly promotional category. Marketing/brand teams kept separate; commercial/department-level synergies captured. Brands complementary in attracting new consumers and expanding usage occasions; opportunities in cooler strategies and greater retailer leverage to win shelf space (energy is impulse-driven - within six feet of a register matters).
Merits of the current dual system (Celsius via PepsiCo/Suntory, Alani Nu via ABI) vs. consolidating Alani Nu into Pepsi, and how the company approaches distribution decisions.

Both ABI and Pepsi systems are highly capable. Pepsi has been a great North American partner (priority periods, suggested/pallet orders, data connections, Subway and college distribution). PepsiCo's CEO referenced active discussions, but it is too early - no decisions on the path forward. Focus is execution, driving share, and capturing the ~$50M synergies; Alani Nu performing well in the ABI system.
Whether the synergies are independent of any distribution consideration.
Confirmed - the company is comfortable with the $50M of synergies regardless of whether North American distribution is dual or single.
Whether, if the dual system remains, the ABI and Pepsi networks can be made to cooperate as well as a single system.

Both networks have pros and cons and are amazing routes to market; the company will keep evaluating what is best for the brands and shareholders, focused on share growth, bringing in consumers, growing the category and selling more cans. The acquisition financials are based on existing partners, distribution and customers.
The right number of SKUs given heavy flavor innovation and the complexity it creates.

The company reviews SKUs annually; SKU consistency is 'a big opportunity' since flavors vary by retailer, and the goal is a consistent in-store flow. Revenue-management capability and Pepsi-network knowledge support prioritization; the company 'cuts its tail' and has shifted from regional lead launches toward national launches while continuing to introduce new flavors annually.
Whether both portfolios are at the right level of overall SKUs.

The goal is constant efficiency - supply chain always wants fewer SKUs. The company is rebalancing pack sizes, upsizing 12-packs and reducing 4-packs as consumption shifts from convenience impulse purchasing toward large-format pantry purchasing, eliminating some SKUs.
Whether the LTO objective is to reengage base consumers or attract new consumers.
The LTO strategy is to attract new consumers - disrupting the path to purchase, bringing Celsius to more people, targeting consumers of other established brands, driving trial.
The drivers of differences between Alani Nu's reported results and consumption data, and any known gaps to expect over the balance of the year.

The LTO strategy makes launches visible quarterly - a launch followed by ~60 days of pickup then a trail-off, with the LTO designed to raise the base. More peaks and valleys for Alani Nu; a pipe-fill spike is recorded in financial results followed by a couple-week delay before it hits scanner data, so within a quarter the gap is unnoticeable but cross-month timing requires keeping investors informed.
How the powder, snack-bar, shake and other alternative businesses fit alongside the core can, and how much focus they get.

The on-the-go powder offering is a great, growing business. Pre-workout/powders are a growth opportunity. Alani Nu's RTD protein is a ~$50M business at scale - a good growth channel with somewhat lower margin that improves with scale, under evaluation over the next couple of years. Smaller protein bars/supplements are less interesting than powders and RTD protein. GLP-1 broadens acceptance of better-for-you energy and protein.
Celsius's Right to Play in Protein / Adjacencies
Whether the Celsius brand has the right to go into protein/adjacencies.

Hydration is another area where Celsius has a right to play - it just launched hydration on-the-go powders in the US, including in Walmart, with strong major-retailer interest. Celsius has a right to play in adjacencies; the hydration product tastes good and has expansion opportunity, letting consumers drink more Celsius throughout the day (since caffeine limits all-day energy-drink consumption).
